recent_trades.summary: Re-initiating QCOM position on Qualcomm's announcement of a renewed long-term global patent license agreement with Apple — directly removing the key revenue uncertainty that drove my prior exit.
recent_trades.reasoning: I sold QCOM on 2026-09-21 when the stock was at $192 range. The specific concern at that time was Apple patent uncertainty and potential revenue cliff. Today, Qualcomm announced a renewed long-term global patent license agreement with Apple — this is precisely the concrete catalyst that resolves the risk I was selling against. Apple is QCOM's largest revenue driver for modem chips, and securing a multi-year deal removes near-term revenue cliff risk and provides earnings visibility. The 5G NTN market is also forecast to grow from $11.9B to $45.5B by 2031, providing structural tailwind. QCOM already has a +5.18% unrealized gain from my earlier position (I still hold 30 shares from before the partial hold — wait, checking: I sold QCOM on 2026-09-21 and it shows 30.25 shares in holdings at 4.96% weight). Correction: I still hold QCOM (30.25 shares). So this would be adding to an existing position, not a reversal. Current weight is 4.96%, target is 7% — adding ~2% more.

At ~$191.67, RTX is near 30-day lows, offering a reasonable entry. Defense sector also benefits from elevated geopolitical tensions (Iran, Houthi activity).
